SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Seneca Resources Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-23
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 887193
Permit API: 083-57162
Unconventional: Yes
County: McKean
Municipality: Sergeant Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-23
Comments: At 17:48 on Saturday (6/20/20), Doug Kepler reported a hose rupture on well pad D08-O that resulted in the discharge of 110-120 barrels of production fluid to containment. Doug Kepler reported about 8-10 barrels of fluid overflowed containment onto a gravel road. It was determined that the spill flowed for 3-4 minutes prior to being noted and then shut off. At the time of this inspection, the operator was in the process of removing the contaminated soil from the impacted area. The containment was vacuumed dry and then removed. A mini excavator and rolloff containers were brought on site. Screening was done of the impacted soil using a soil conductivity meter with a probe. It was determined that the production water flowed along the access road approximately 200-250 feet in a narrow band before exiting the road surface in a small depression. The operator had removed all the impacted soil in this stretch at the time of this inspection. They were loading their 11th container at this time. An excavation was developing deeper on the northeast side of the spill site, where elevated conductivity was noted several feet into the soil. The operator will continue to screen and remove soil today and for as long as necessary. Rolloff containers are being staged on the D08-O pad, which is just off the edge of the spill location. Further follow up of this spill location will be performed as necessary.

Comments: On December 12 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Adams 877-5 OG Well Site in regards to violatons issued under IR 3609158.The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, The stained gravel beneath the valve on the production tank did not appear to be present. Upon removing the initial layer of gravel, no stained gravel was uncovered. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.28mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the location of the spill with readings of 2.53mS, 1.35mS, and 2.07mS. Although it appears efforts have been made to remediate the release, conductivity readings are still elevated in comparison to the background reading. The Department recommends the operator assess the well site to ensure it has been properly remediated. The Department has yet to receive the information requested in IR 3609158. The Department also requests waste manifests for the impacted material that was removed. Based on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/05/2025
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8236897
Permit API: 129-24171
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/05/2025
Comments: On June 5, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 well located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following Complaint Inspection 3891447 where violations were issued for inadequate stabilization of the direct and shared portions of the access road that leads to the Armstrong 2 site. A notice of violation (NOV) operator response has yet to be received from the Operator of this Oil and Gas well following IR 3891447, however, a NOV response was received for a nearby well site operated by a separate Operator that received the same violations for the shared portion of the Armstrong 2's access road, and that NOV response stated that repairs to the shared portion of the road would be conducted in the Spring of 2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the condition of the shared portion of Wildcat Road to be unchanged, major rutting and erosion rills were observed throughout.Wildcat Road eventually leads to a fork, left leading to another well site (the James Armstrong Jr 1), and right leading directly to the Armstrong 2 well site. Along the direct portions of the Armstrong 2 well site, the Department observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised. The Department is requesting within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report, a written timeline of access road remedial actions for both the shared and direct portions of the access road.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be completely overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observe fixed to a heavily rusted wellhead with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. A heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank to ensure the corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road shall remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: 10/2/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an administrative inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected during drilling operations from two different locations at the site.During inspection #4038825, conducted on 8/21/2025, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of thepad. Liquid draining from the north center outfall into the basin field tested at 1983 uS conductance. Sample 9551-219 was collected from this area. The liquid in the pond next to the northeast overflow weir field tested at 1924 uS conductance. Sample 9551220 was collected from this area.On 9/19/2025, the department received the results of the samples. The results are supplied in the photographs.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.

Violation ID: 877385

Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene

Inspection Date: 2020-02-18
Comments: On 02/14/2020 WQS Kristof Eichenlaub conducted incident response inspection # 2999089 On 02/18/2020 at approximately 1350 I conducted a follow up inspection at the site. Foamer product and sediment laden water were discharging from the sediment basin outlet, overwhelming two silt socks, and discharging outside the LOD into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. The discharge caused accelerated erosion below the silt socks and extending into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A contractor for Greylock was utilizing a bucket and a pressurized sprayer bottle in an attempt to remove foamer product from the sediment basin rip rap outlet. I inquired what the contractor was utilizing to eliminate the foam. The contractor informed me they were utilizing fabric softener. I contacted Greylock Regulatory Compliance Coordinator Keith Eighmey via phone, who indicated he was unaware of the contractor's activities. Eighmey indicated Greylock had previously utilized a defoaming agent in the channels and basin to eliminate foamer product. Eighmey indicated Greylock could provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The Department requests Greylock provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The spill had not been remediated and was continuing to discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A sediment laden water discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run was also continuing. Greylock discharged an additional substance to Waters of the Commonwealth during their attempt to remove the foamer. Some violations are ongoing as a result of a spill that was documented on 02/14/2020 (inspection # 2999089). Additional violations of CSL 301 and 307 have occurred due to Greylock discharging a chemical to UNT 8 to reduce the surfactant foam. A violation of OGA3259(2I) has occurred for failure to comply with DEP cleanup order issued on 02/14/2020.

Comments: On 12/12/2022, I conducted a follow up inspection of the DR02 Pad and Impoundment ESX 1H well. Nucomer has hired a 3rd party contractor "Assist" to complete the secondary containment liner repair. TJ Pennino from EMKEY Gathering was on site representing Nucomer Energy. This is in response to violations in previous inspections(3459581). The violations are for tears and holes in the secondary containment liner in the tank battery. Two different methods were being utilized in the repair attempt. One is a hot air weld of liner material. The second was a PVC extruder gun as seen in photo #3. It should be noted the original containment liner is thickness of 20 mil. The patch material brought by Assist for the hot air welding is a 40 mil thickness. After several attempts to hot air weld the patch material to the existing liner, it was evident trying to weld the 40 mil patch material to the 20 mil existing material was not going to work. Several pieces of the 20 mil liner were cut from outside containment and cleaned as best as possible. Again the original liner material is too thin and was not supporting a good hot-air weld. The extruder was used on several smaller holes. It became obvious it is not suitable to be used on a material of this thickness. The temperature was set as low as the machine would allow and the material melted through the original liner (pictures #1 and #4).After several attempts trying several different methods, the decision was made by TJ to abandon the repair attempt. TJ was going to speak with ASSIST and plan another course of action and discuss options available.Additionally the violation for the 55 gallon drums being stored outside of secondary containment, can be closed. This violation has been resolved.

Comments: On Wednesday, 12/14/2022, I conducted a routine inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The well is in production and had a reported production of 5,341.89 mcf for 2021. There is a well id tag attached to the well head and a well site id sign is posted on the production chart box. The site is restored, but the operator has not maintained the E and S BMP's for the site and there is an area of standing/ponded water on the access road near the site entrance (see picture #8) that needs to be addressed. The site cannot be considered stabilized due to this area and also the area of dead vegetation that was caused by brine being sprayed from a broken pipe onto the brine tank and ground. The brine tank itself is stable and appears to be structurally sound, but the pipe into the brine tank from the gas separator has rusted through and broken off, spraying brine onto the outside of the tank and onto the ground (see pictures #6 and #7). The amount of brine released appears to be less than 1 bbl. These conditions have resulted in violations to 25 PA Code 78.57(a), 25 PA Code 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1) and CSL 402(b) being cited. Although there were no violations cited, the deficiencies on the access road need to be addressed while the operator is addressing the conditions that resulted in the cited violations.

Comments: On February 25, 2026, the Department conducted a Site Restoration Inspection of Diversified's Chess 19 plugged well site located in Georges Township, Fayette County following the 1/14/2026 receipt of a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR).A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2026. According to the COA, the Operator is to restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 8/21/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 5/21/2026, and a WSRR should be submitted to the Department by 7/20/2026. The status of the COA is discussed in IR 4152827.At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe a Post-Plugging Site Restoration Plan on-site. Violations are being issued at this time.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a dirt and partially graveled shared access road leading to a partially vegetated and graveled direct access road. The direct access road was not observed to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth, however it was observed to be thoroughly seeded and mulched. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the plugged well site to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Mulch from what appears to be removed Compost Filter Sock was observed to be spread along the edges of the plugged well site. No erosion and sediment controls were observed to be installed on site at the time of this inspection.At the time of this inspection, the Department traveled to the approximate GPS coordinate location of the plugged well and did not observe any fluid leaks or fluid discharges coming from the surface of this location.Based on today's inspection, the Department is recommending the WSRR be returned as the access road does not appear to be restored. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to have a Post-Plugging Site Restoration Plan on site. Future violations may be forthcoming dependent upon the complete restoration of the plugged well site and access road by 5/21/2026 and the re-submittal of a WSRR by 7/20/2026.

Comments: On site inspection of clean-up of a <30 gallon release of produced fluid (brine water and crude oil) from tanks set on site. Clean stone was brought and piled on site in dump truck to be used to haul out contaminated stone and clay. The mini excavator was used to scrape saturated stone and clay into a pile and load into lined dump truck. The depression left from the clean-up has oily water left in it. Mr. Cochran is going to use a pump and tank to removed remaining water in the depression to be disposed of at a licensed facility. The contaminated stone and clay to be taken to landfill in McKean. The depression left from the clean-up will be backfilled with some type of clean stone material and stone on site. A single layer of rough cut boards were placed as deck of bridge. Dump truck and mini excavator used bridge to access well. Mr. Cochran stated that a second layer of boards will be put down and side rails attached to complete the bridge deck. Gravel to be put on the either side of the bridge.Remaining violations to be lifted when clean-up is completed and bridge repair completed.

Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

Comments: On March 25, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3484420, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2, 4, and 5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head closest to the well head was observed on the ground. The Department recommends that this top hatch is replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater (see photo 6).The well postings on-site include contact information for Murphy Production, Inc. The well tag is affixed to the well head with Murphy Production Inc listed on the tag along with the permit number and well name (see photo 8, 11, and 13).No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 10). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 9). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site.The access road is stabilized with gravel. The well is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 3 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued under IR 3484420 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/19/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/19/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 992327
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 2.60 mS/cm. Multiple seeps were observed coming from the well pad side slope and the topsoil stockpile which were flowing into the sump. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Seneca Resources Co Llc in Jones Twp, Elk County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-07-11 to Seneca Resources Co Llc in Jones Twp, Elk county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Seneca Resources Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-07-11
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 855341
Permit API: 047-24967
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-11
Comments: The operator reported to DEP on 7/10/19 that a 1-2 barrel spill of production fluid occurred at the E09 S well pad. This inspection occurred the morning of 7/11. It appears as though a fitting on a dump line from a bulk unit failed, which allowed produced water to spill into the containment within the unit. Once the containment of approximately 600 gallons was filled, water began to spill out on either side of the unit. Workers on site noticed the spill and immediately shut the site down so that containment and remediation could begin. It is estimated that 1-2 barrels of production fluid was spilled to the ground. Equipment was brought to the site and three roll-off containers were filled with contaminated soil. The operator used a soil probe to determine where conductivity was elevated and dug an area approximately 30x60 feet at the time of this inspection. They did not dig under the bulk unit, as they were going to attempt to flush any production fluid out from under it rather than move the unit at this time. Work will continue on this site until soil tests come back clean. No threats to nearby water sources were noted, as this spill was contained within a small area on the pad.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/07/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8154569
Permit API: 033-23894
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Ferguson Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/07/2023
Comments: Diversified Prod LLC reported a brine spill to the Department on August 3, 2023 which occurred at conventional well 033-23894. I conducted a site inspection on August 7, 2023 and met with Diversified EHS Specialist's Paul Stiner and Will Warfel. Diversified has delineated the impacted area to be approximately 30' x 40'. They have installed E and S controls downslope of the excavation area. Diversified started excavation on August 5, 2023. Impacted soils were placed on plastic. Due to heavy rainfalls during my inspection the operator has postponed excavation. A dump truck was onsite upon my arrival and was loaded with impacted soils. Soils are being hauled offsite to Carbon Limestone Landfill in Ohio. Fluids with in the brine tank have been vacuumed out and properly disposed. According to Mr. Stiner, all fluids will be removed and the brine tank will be moved in order to excavate impacted soils. I randomly screened within the delineated impacted area with a Hanna Gro Line Soil Tester. Readings exceeded 4.0 mS/cm which is the maximum conductivity reading for this soil probe. Additional screenings were conducted outside the delineated area and the readings were not elevated. A soil sample was collected (3442694) and was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg to be tested for SAC 530 plus, bromide, lithium, and strontium. Diversified is planning to go through the Act 2 for site remediation. Moody Environmental has been hired to assist them for site remediation. Violations have been cited.

The Department recommends removing all impacted soil and properly disposing. The Department requests that the quantity released, composition of fluids released, how the release occurred, and when the release occurred is included in the NOV response. The Department requests disposal documents of the impacted material removed from the site, when made available. The Department recommends properly disposing of trash.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review drill cuttings processing activity and overall site conditions. Meeting on site with Seneca Company Man Wesley Sammons. Weather conditions are partly cloudy and 58 degrees F.According to Mr. Sammons, the Patterson 801 rig is drilling the lateral on thr 74HU well (API # 117-22221) well at the Taft pad. This is the fourth well of five being drilled to Total Depth. There are no pre-existing wells at this location. The rig is currently drilling at a depth of around 20,674' on synthetic oil based mud (OBM) and the TD is expected at 26,554'. Cementing of the production casing is expected to take place on June 2. Seneca submitted a Request for Approval of Previously Approved Alternative Waste Management Practices (OG-71) Form Bapplication for the Taft 851 Pad on 1/24/24. The Department approved the request on 1/24/24. The request for the approval of Alternative Waste Management Practices is for drill cuttings processing and solids removal from drilling mud. See photos and comments in the on-site processing findings section of this inspection report below, and refer to the Beechwood C08-G OG-71 Form A application, which was approved by the Department on 9/22/20, EFACTS Authorization ID#1327841.White's Energy Services is handling drill cuttings solidification and loadout in the rig backyard. There are no chemicals in use to facilitate cuttings processing in the backyard during OBM drilling. Drilling fluid is removed from cuttings using drying shakers and a series of centrifuges to remove solids from the reusable drilling mud. The rig mats, steel rolloffs, and equipment in the backyard area are clean and free of debris. The site is well organized. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum containment water from duck pads and tertiary containment structures to ensure adequate capacity in case of heavy precipitation. Violations remain outstanding against permit #117-22231 for pollutional water found on site and documented in Inspection Reports #3736567 and #3724668. There are no new violations noted.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8187542

Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Fawn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/13/2024
Comments: On May 13, 2024 the Department conducted an incident inspection in regards to a spill that occurred at the Sun Mine Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued on 9/11/2023 and expires on 9/10/2028) on May 10, 2024. According to Derek Zofchak of Range Resources, the spill occurred at 12 PM when drill cuttings and soap slurry fluid entered the flare stack eco tank (which normally separates fluids from gas), the float on the pump within the eco tank malfunctioned and as a result, fluid (approximately 30 gallons of drill cuttings and soap slurry) that normally would not get carried over to the flare stack ended up spewing out of the flare stack as a fine mist onto the graveled well pad and well pad fill slope. At the time of the inspection, Range Resources notified the Department that the spill had been remediated. Two roll off dumpsters were on site filled with waste material, the well pad appeared to be scraped on the left hand side of the flare stack, and new seed and mulch was seen on the the fill slope and berm directly in front of and to the left-hand side of the flare stack.
